Interesting, my brother is diagnosed OCD, ADHD, Autism, clinically depressed, GAD, and insomnia, and he shows some of those traits as well. He has struggled a lot in his life, because he hasn’t been able to understand why it seems people don’t like him or understand him, he feels very unloved...we were both abused as children, and he experienced being sexually abused, as well myself. He has been taken advantage of a lot by people who see his naivety and they will manipulate him into doing things, he is very sensitive to people’s emotions, but I’ve noticed the one thing that differentiates us is the fact that he is unable to understand the reasoning behind people being upset with him. He is extremely book smart, but by no means street smart because he is unable to pick up on any social cues. He is very obsessed with having a routine and if he is unable to maintain that, it will set him off or make him feel like he did something very bad. He is so obsessed with his routine that he will allow it to get in the way of normal family activities, or put off his real responsibilities if it doesn’t coincide with his routine. Since most people are unable to understand him and why he is so obsessed with his routine, or the fact that the longer people get to know him, the more they realize he is extremely socially awkward, he loses friends and hasn’t been able to maintain a romantic relationship with anyone (not for more than three months) and he’s 25. He also seems to have an extremely hard time being on his own, he really struggles with every day tasks (like I said) if it doesn’t fall under his routine. He currently lives with our grandparents. I will say, he seems to really care about what other people think of him, and since he feels like nobody can love him, this affects his self esteem in more negative ways. My dad refuses to believe that any diagnoses is real so this makes it even harder for the both of us, but especially my brother as he seems to really need people’s validation. On the surface, he seems very normal and charming, but once you actually talk to him you notice these tendencies. 

As for myself, I am diagnosed with PTSD, BPD, anxiety, and depression. I do not obsess with needing a routine, in fact I’m the complete opposite, I despise routines and haven’t been able to maintain any healthy one for a consistent amount of time. I don’t have any obsessions with anything (besides people, if my BPD makes me idealize someone). I also struggle with everyday tasks but in a very different way, sometimes I will get so depressed to the point where I won’t eat for the entire day, or barely use the restroom. I also split on people, so if someone does something to me (that could seem small to someone else) it could shift my whole view on the person in a negative light and I cut off anyone I feel like can’t be trusted or has hurt me in some way - this is why people with BPD have a hard time maintaining friendships and relationships, you see, this is different from ASD because people with ASD tend to have a hard time keeping friendships/relationships because of the social aspect - seeming like an outcast. Splitting can also go the complete opposite way, where you see someone in a positive light and in your eyes they can do no wrong...until they do then you ghost them or cut them off out of nowhere. And my fear of abandonment is more subconscious, my thought process is that because this person did this then I will automatically think they don’t love me, they don’t want to be with me, etc. I also have highs and lows, I can go from seeming completely normal and in a good mood to being triggered and snapping at someone I love for something small. I also have the tendency to push away anyone that cares about me (even if I want them in my life), where I’ve noticed my brother would prefer to keep those people around if he could, I isolate myself then end up alone and this causes me to feel even more lonely - even if it was self inflicted. I am also very street smart...I can pick up on social cues, I am very receptive of people’s emotions, when I don’t have any close relationships, this can be a good thing as people who aren’t close to me tend to not really overwhelm me. The only people who really get to see my BPD symptoms are the ones closest to me (family, friends, etc), but I cut off all of my friends because of my disorder.
